title: Tom Brady and the Act of Signing Autographs for Teammates
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece uses Tom Brady's late-career habit of signing memorabilia for teammates to make a point about motivating people. Even his Tampa Bay teammates were in awe of him, and they left items in the locker next to his hoping he would sign them for friends and family. He signed them all, often spending hours and adding personal notes. The author reads this as a secret of motivation: signing signaled to teammates' families how highly Brady regarded them, raising the teammates' standing in loved ones' eyes. The general principle is that leaders who make colleagues look special or influential to the people they care about create a bond that is hard to break. The piece ends by asking when the reader last did this for someone at work.
points: Brady's willingness to sign whatever teammates left shows a star using his status to elevate others.
Making people look special in the eyes of friends and family inspires them and bonds them to the leader.
No one asks to be made to look special, which is why leaders who do it unprompted inspire so strongly.
The test for the reader is to recall the last time they made a colleague look that special.
quotes: By the time future Hall of Fame Quarterback Tom Brady was nearing retirement, he was famous even among his new teammates on the Tampa Bay team where he played his last three seasons. Believed to be the Greatest of All Time (GOAT) at the quarterback position, even his fellow NFL colleagues were in awe of his record and status.

Brady never disappointed. He was happy to place his signature on whatever item was left for him and with a note to whoever his teammates directed him to write to. He often spent hours signing the mementos with one idea in mind.

Beyond being a good guy and teammate, Brady knew a secret of motivation and inspiration. Making people look special in the eyes of their friends and family inspired them and created a bond between him and each player which would last for years.

That he would go out of his way to offer his autograph to whatever was left for him to sign was a signal to the friends and families of his colleagues. It said loudly that his teammates were held in high esteem by him. In the eyes of those on the receiving end of the mementos, they didn’t just think highly of Brady. They now knew the special status of his prized teammate.

Making others look special or influential in the eyes of those they care about creates a connection between leaders and teammates that can’t be easily broken. While no one would explicitly ask to be made to look special or influential, when leaders elevate the specialness of team members or colleagues in the eyes of others, they inspire them in a way nothing else can.
